overview: After 1.d4 Nf6 2.c4 c5 3.d5 b5 White does not accept with cxb5 but plays the aggressive 4.g4, attacking the knight and threatening g5. Black can take ...Nxg4 and win a pawn, or play ...bxc4 first. White plays for rapid attack and development in return. A rare anti-Benko, aggressive but risky.

white_ideas.idea: Push g5 and h4 to chase the knight and attack the kingside.
Use Bg2 and Rg1 and the open g-file to attack.

black_ideas.idea: Take on g4 or play ...bxc4 first to keep the extra material.
Counter in the centre with ...e6 or ...d6 and ...Bb7 on the long diagonal.

typical_structures.structure: White space with d5 and g4 against Black's ...c5/...b5 wing play, and kings possibly castling opposite.

character.notes: White throws the g-pawn forward and both sides take risks.

gambit.notes: White offers the g4 pawn and Black can keep it.

soundness.notes: An anti-Benko sideline that is not considered to give enough for the material.

structure.notes: Black's c5/b5 pawns against White's d5 and g4 with an unsettled centre.

approach.notes: Very seldom played by strong players; chosen for surprise.

level.notes: Aggressive but dubious, so never Beginner.
